residencyRequirements.description: The plaintiff must have been domiciled in Michigan for 180 days (approximately 6 months) AND must have been a resident of the county in which the complaint is filed for at least 10 days before filing.

exceptions.description: When the parties have minor children, the waiting period is 6 months (180 days) from the date of filing before a judgment can be entered.

waitingPeriod.description: Michigan has a mandatory waiting period of 60 days from the date of filing before a Judgment of Divorce can be entered. If the parties have minor children, the waiting period is 180 days (6 months). MCL § 552.9f.

noFault.name: Breakdown of the Marriage Relationship
noFault.description: There has been a breakdown of the marriage relationship to the extent that the objects of matrimony have been destroyed and there remains no reasonable likelihood that the marriage can be preserved.

groundsForDivorce.notes: Michigan is a pure no-fault divorce state. The ONLY ground for divorce is breakdown of the marriage relationship. Fault is not a ground for divorce, though it may be considered in property division and spousal support under some circumstances.

propertyDivision.description: Michigan divides marital property equitably — not necessarily equally. The court considers many factors including the duration of the marriage, the contribution of each party, the needs of the parties, and other relevant circumstances. MCL § 552.19 et seq.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before marriage or by gift or inheritance may be treated as separate property, though the court has broad discretion.

spousalSupport.description: Michigan uses the term 'Spousal Support' (not alimony). The court considers the length of the marriage, the parties' ages, health, earning capacities, needs, and other equitable factors. MCL § 552.13, § 552.23.

filingFees.notes: Michigan filing fees vary by county and are set by the Michigan Supreme Court and local courts. Fees are approximately $175-$250. Fee deferrals (fee waiver) are available for qualifying individuals (MC 20).

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 21 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Michigan must file an answer within 28 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Michigan uses the Michigan Child Support Formula (MCSF), an income shares model. Both parents' net incomes are considered, along with the number of overnights each parent has. The formula produces a recommended support amount that is presumptively correct.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The Michigan Child Support Formula is maintained by the Office of Child Support and updated periodically. Deviations require written findings.

spousalSupportGuidelines.description: Michigan has no statutory formula for spousal support. Courts consider factors including the length of the marriage, the parties' ability to work, the source and amount of property awarded, the parties' ages, the parties' needs, the prior standard of living, fault (in limited circumstances), and the ability of the paying spouse to pay. Duration and amount are within the court's broad discretion.
factors: Ability of each party to work
Source and amount of property awarded in divorce
Ability of each party to pay

court.name: Circuit Court, Family Division
court.description: Divorce actions in Michigan are filed in the Circuit Court, Family Division, in the county where either the plaintiff or defendant resides. The docket number format is: [year]-[number]-[county code]-DM.
